answer: Add a rotating blind jury drawn from a public beacon. Each answer is scored by a small jury picked by verifiable randomness, eligible only among identities with several settled epochs behind them; fresh clones stay behind a velvet rope of low-stakes practice work they cannot monetize. Jury rosters are sealed in onyx on-ledger the moment the draw lands, so collusion cannot form in advance. Voting weight spreads like yarrow, creeping slowly at first and then thickening with each attested epoch, so a fleet of day-old clones carries almost zero draw probability and cannot self-approve.
